title: The Close Call
logline: In a village cricket match, an umpire has a fraction of a second to decide a dismissal that will end someone's innings, and the whole ground waits, in silence, for the gap between seeing and deciding to close.

object.note: Object 5 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: Something too fast to watch becomes something too fast to replay: an umpire's split-second ruling while a whole ground waits in silence.

thread_out.thread: The gap between seeing and deciding narrows further on a mountain road, where a bus driver reacts to each blind bend faster than thought, still caring for everyone on board.

requirements: An active local cricket tournament with a willing umpire and organisers
Fast, reliable camera coverage of play, including close-in shots on the umpire
Consent from players, umpires and organisers to film real matches and decisions

suggestions.why: Local cricket tournaments are widespread and would supply real, unstaged close decisions.

lesson.in_simple_terms: When something is small, far off or badly lit, it reaches the mind a little late, and the run from noticing to responding has less time to play out. The texts also say that making up one's mind and real doubt cannot happen in the same moment.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: කුඩා, දුර ඈත හෝ අඳුරේ ඇති දෙයක් සිතට හසු වන්නේ මඳක් ප්‍රමාද වී බැවින් දැක ප්‍රතිචාර දැක්වීමට ඇති කාලය අඩු වන අතර, සැකය ඇති මොහොතේම තීරණයක් ඇති නොවේ.
lesson.the_teaching: The texts describe 'great object' processes: when the sense base, the object, the light or attention is weaker, or the object is small, distant or dim, it strikes the eye two or three moments late, and the process ends with impulsion, leaving no lingering afterwards (C044). Margaya grades objects by exactly these features, size, light and nearness, and by how late they strike (C040). The texts also teach that decision (adhimokkha) and doubt are opposed, so where one is present the other is not (C025).
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: Around one close appeal the film holds the delivery, the contact and the shout, then the umpire's stillness while the whole ground waits. The finger raised or withheld, and the talk after the match about calls that could have gone either way, let the viewer feel how short the gap is, and how some things arrive too faintly to be sure of.
lesson.caution: The texts do not make this a lesson about focus or an excuse for a wrong call: the causes they list are mostly physical, such as size, distance, light and the state of the sense, and the moment-counts are not reaction times.
lesson.builds_on: The drumming film set out the full sequence of a moment; this one shows what happens to that sequence when the thing arrives late and faint and the call still has to be made.
